evidence: Created a standalone GPL-3.0-only Rust download-engine crate using tokio and reqwest within the permitted packages path.

Behavioral runtime tests used controlled local HTTP servers and passed segmented Range transfer and Range-ignored single-stream fallback scenarios, comparing completed files byte-for-byte with a 32,000-byte source payload.
The Range-supporting runtime test observed at least five Range requests: one capability probe and four bounded segment transfers.

Implemented concurrent bounded segment requests with a maximum of eight segments, exact segment-length validation, positioned reassembly, final-length verification, and publication through part-file rename.
Implemented atomic JSON manifest replacement, per-segment completed-byte checkpoints, and startup conversion of active state to recoverably_interrupted.
Behavioral persistence test passed with a simulated active manifest retaining a four-byte segment checkpoint across reload.
Behavioral filename tests passed for path traversal removal, invalid Windows-character replacement, and Windows reserved-name handling.
URL intake rejects non-HTTP(S) schemes, missing hosts, and embedded credentials before network activity.
Final cargo test passed 2 integration tests with zero failures; unit and documentation test targets also passed.
Final cargo clippy completed successfully with warnings denied.
Final git diff --check exited successfully; output contained only pre-existing LF-to-CRLF warnings for .gitignore and engineering/taskboard/workstreams.csv.
knownRisks: Pause, resume, cancel, queued-download orchestration, live progress metrics, and resumable HTTP continuation are not yet wired into a long-running engine service; this crate currently provides durable state primitives and complete-transfer execution.
The Tauri command adapter and Windows open/reveal, folder-picker, and clipboard adapters remain integration dependencies outside the implemented package.

The authoritative write boundary excludes root Cargo.toml and LICENSE, so this crate cannot yet be registered in a root Rust workspace and the required root GPL-3.0 text could not be added by this workstream.
Downloads without a trustworthy Content-Length are not supported robustly because final validation currently relies on a known total length.
Redirect targets are restricted only by reqwest's redirect-count policy; per-hop scheme, host, and private-network policy requires further security hardening.

The implementation buffers each concurrently downloaded segment in memory before positioned file writes, so large files can consume excessive memory; streaming each segment directly to separate part files is recommended before release.
Independent engineering verification remains reserved for ENG-15.
